Get dimensions of a LaTeX expression

Source: R/latex-grob.R
latex_dims.Rd

Get dimensions of a LaTeX expression

Usage

latex_dims(
  tex,
  fontsize = 20,
  line_space = 10,
  max_width = 0,
  render_mode = c("typeface", "path")
)

Arguments

tex

Character string of LaTeX math code.

fontsize

Base font size in points (default: 20).

line_space

Numeric inter-line spacing in big points for multi-line formulas (e.g., \\, \begin{array}). Default is 10.

max_width

Numeric maximum width in big points for automatic line wrapping. Use 0 (default) for no wrapping.

render_mode

Character string: "typeface" (default) renders glyphs as native text using the math font, producing selectable/accessible text in PDF and SVG output. Requires the math font to be installed on the system. Falls back to path mode automatically on devices that do not support font embedding (e.g., the base pdf() device). "path" renders math symbols as filled vector paths (works on all devices but text is not selectable in PDF/SVG). For PDF output with embedded/selectable text, prefer cairo_pdf.

Value

A list with width, height, depth, and baseline as grid unit objects.

Examples

latex_dims("\\frac{a}{b}")
#> $width
#> [1] 8bigpts
#> 
#> $height
#> [1] 21bigpts
#> 
#> $depth
#> [1] 7bigpts
#> 
#> $baseline
#> [1] 0.6662558
#>
